disposition_reason: A short risk-assessment report that compiles arsenic, lead, cadmium and mercury results posted by nine US baby food manufacturers (1362 products) and computes hazard quotients; the authors did no measurements and the main text gives only brand-level ranges across mixed product types (pouches, snacks, meals).

study.design: Risk interpretation of manufacturer-posted test results (secondary compilation)
study.market: US baby food sold by nine manufacturers with web-posted results

period.as_reported: results extracted from manufacturer websites in September 2025 (sample dates not given)

study.method: Not stated; manufacturer laboratory results as posted (ppb)
lod: LODs mostly undisclosed; California AB 899 requires LOD no greater than 6 ppb

unresolved: Table 1 brand-level ranges (e.g. brand B cadmium <LOD to 108 ppb, lead <LOD to 13 ppb; brand E arsenic 7.1-58.9 ppb) are manufacturer-posted values pooled across mixed product types; not recorded as findings because they are secondary data without product categories.
Arsenic species (total vs inorganic) not stated for the posted results.
Product-level database is in a Supplementary file not available with the PDF.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: US FDA action level for lead in processed foods for babies and young children

regulatory_or_exposure.value: NSRL µg/day: As 10, Pb 15, Cd 0.05; MADL µg/day: Pb 0.5, Cd 4.1, Hg 0.3

regulatory_or_exposure.what: US EPA RfD (iAs, Cd) and EFSA TDI (inorganic Hg)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: iAs 0.3, Cd 1.0, Hg 0.57 µg/kg bw/day; child body weight 11.4 kg

regulatory_or_exposure.what: California AB 899 maximum LOD for baby food testing
